courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: So we enabled the Google Maps APIs,
let's now add maps to our project.
Now we could grab that import for the Javascript SDK and in our project, we could add that to the
index.html file
but that would always load the entire Google Maps Javascript SDK even if we're not using it yet
and therefore this is actually not the approach I will use,
instead we'll dynamically import this when we need it.
So for that, let's go back to our code and there let's plan which kind of components we now need or what
we want to add.
Now my goal is that when we create a new offer,
so on this new offer page, in the existing form which we already have below our date inputs,
I actually want to add a new input, a custom input which allows the user to click on a button let's
say
and later on a preview of the location
and that should open up a modal which presents a map where we can pick a location and later in the next
section where we tap into native device features, we will actually also add an option to autolocate
the user.
So I want to be able to pick a location on a map and therefore, we'll have to add our own form control
so to say, our own component that allows us to do just that
and hence I will add this.
So here in my Ionic project, I'll use ionic generate component and generate a new component which we
can use as that form control that allows us to pick a map and I want to store that in let's say the
shared folder and there under pickers and of course, the path is totally up to you
and I'll name this location-picker
and again you can name this however you want and store this wherever you want but in the end, that kind
of describes what it is and I store it in a shared folder because we could use that application wide in
any form where we need a picker for a map.
Now that location picker is in the end the component that should present a button and a preview of the
map snippet we picked later that allows the user to tap and then open up a modal.
Now for the modal that should open up, I'll generate another component and let's say we do that just under
shared here, the map-modal component, that will be the component that holds the actual map and that
opens in a modal and that will be the place where we then also import Google Maps API or that Google
Maps Javascript SDK later.
So with these two components added here in the shared folder, let's continue and let's actually start
by ensuring that we open that modal as fast as possible before we then focus on adding the logic for the
user to click there and select the location.
So on the location picker here, I'll start really simple by adding a div that should wrap basically
my entire picker logic and in the div here, I want to have an ion-button where I say select location
and that button will receive a color of primary let's say and yes, that doesn't sound too bad.
Now when this button gets clicked, I'll fire or I'll trigger the onPickLocation method here and inside
of the button, I actually also want to show an icon let's say, so let's also add an ion-icon here with
a name of map and the slot should be start so that this is nicely positioned in the button and let's
wrap the text in an ion-label,
not necessarily required but let's still do that to make sure that all the styling works out correctly.
So now we added this button with the icon and the label in there,
now with that added, we can add the onPickLocation method here to the location picker component and
that should be the method that actually opens up that modal that displays the map thereafter.
Now if you want to load a modal or display a modal, you know what that means, we have to inject the modal
controller, modal controller which we import from @ionic/angular,
that is what we did before in this application as well
and now here, I will use the modal controller and call create to create a new modal.
Here we now need to specify a component that should be loaded and that should be my map modal component
so let's add it here.
Now before we continue, of course you need to make sure that you added the import but besides that,
we need to make sure that the map modal component is added as an entry component to a module
and speaking of modules, the CLI automatically added the map modal component and the location picker component
to the declarations of the app module.
Now that is actually not the place where I want this because I'll not be using the location picker in my
app component which is the only other component declared here and therefore which is the only component
where I could use that, instead I'll remove the declarations from the app module and I'll add a new
shared module here in my shared folder.
Now the idea behind the shared modules simply is that I can thereafter import that share module into
any component or any other module that wants to use the location picker or the map modal and that gives
us more flexibility.
So here, I'll export a class, shared module and we should add @NgModule here and in there, we can
now add declarations and I want to add my location picker component and the modal, the map modal component
here
and of course add the imports as well
and now I also want to export that,
so the location picker component and the map modal component so that we can use them in any component
or in any modules components that imports that shared module.
I also will add entry components here and add the map modal component there and we'll also add an imports
array because I want to be able to use things like ngIf in these components and therefore we need
to import the common module here from @angular/common. So with all that added, we got the shared module
set up and we can now import the shared module in all the other modules where we plan on using the location
picker or the map modal. With that back to the location picker component,
let's continue working on showing that map modal.
